Subject: Medigen sequencing — MSA / DPA / OF decision gates

Hi Mina / Karthik —

Thanks again for last week's demo. Procurement asked me to capture a clear sequence of approvals so we can present to our legal & security committees next Tuesday. High level asks from procurement: 
- Can we get a concise milestone map that shows which document needs to be signed before we can provision dedicated capacity?
- What are the absolute blockers vs. negotiable items for Go-Live (SLA windows, data residency clause, subprocessor list)?

I attached a draft order form (v3) with quantities. Can your team call out dependencies (e.g., DPA executed -> enable logging export / MSA executed -> billing commences)? We're aiming for a 6–8 week close but need clarity on gating steps.

Appreciate a quick MAP (mutual action plan) we can inline in our board packet.

Claire
Claire Young
Director, Strategic Procurement | Medigen, Inc.

Date: Fri, 20 Jun 2025 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Medigen sequencing — MSA / DPA / OF decision gates

Claire — thanks, clear asks. Draft MAP below — happy to convert to a one-pager for your packet. High-level sequencing (recommended):

1) Security review + DPA finalization (target: Week 1–2)
   - Outcome required to enable audit logging export and KMS key policy.
2) MSA negotiation and operational terms (Week 2–4)
   - MSA needs to be signed prior to committed provisioning and billing.
3) Order Form (quantities, region, start date) sign-off (Week 3–5)
   - Can be signed concurrently with final MSA if legal approves minor OF edits.
4) Provisioning & connectivity (Week 4–6)
   - Dedicated capacity queued once DPA + MSA in place and PO received.
5) Acceptance / data-handling checklist + go/no-go (Week 5–8)

Absolute blockers: DPA execution for data export, explicit regional residency clause (if required by your policy), and mutual SLA on incident RTO for PII. Negotiable: certain OF line-item phrasings (we can accept PO-level billing modifiers).

Action items for your side:
- Legal: review enclosed DPA summary table and flag non-starters by 2025-06-24.
- Procurement: confirm purchase order cadence and whether billing must start on signature vs. provisioning date.

I'll loop Rishi for technical gating and Karthik/Laura for legal/ops redlines. Would you like a short slide we can use in your Tuesday packet?

Thanks —
Mina Haddad
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
Cell: (628) 555-0139
Attachments: none

Subject: Re: Medigen sequencing — MSA / DPA / OF decision gates

TL;DR: technical gating items that require DPA/MSA sign-off before provisioning:
- KMS key holder policy (DPA + KMS policy) -> prevents cross-tenant access during export.
- Logging retention & export window (DPA) -> needed for compliance ingestion.
- Burst capacity SLA (MSA) -> if Medigen expects predictable burst lanes we need explicit commitment window.

We can draft a tight acceptance checklist that ties to the OF line items (token commitment, region, retention). If procurement is okay with provisioning after DPA + a countersigned MSA signature page, we can stage capacity and delay billing until onboarding acceptance to meet their finance ask.

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Claire — attaching our redlines and a DPA summary table to make review quicker. Key notes: 
- We can accept the majority of your OF language; two clauses we need to align on before signature: the refund/credit on SLA breaches and the export scope on subprocessors.
- If Medigen can sign the DPA with an appendix listing required subprocessors, we can parallel-track MSA with commercial terms so you can hit the Week 4 provisioning target.

I've uploaded the redlines and a short one-pager that maps each redline to the MAP milestone. If procurement needs a single doc to present — we recommend the MAP + one-page redline summary.

Karthik Iyer
Legal & Contracts Lead (Commercial) | Redwood Inference
